question: Walk through the PKCE S256 math. Why must the verifier be 43-128 characters, and why is a valid challenge always exactly 43 characters?
answer_hinglish:
PKCE mein client ek random code_verifier banata hai aur /authorize par sirf uska challenge bhejta hai: challenge = BASE64URL(SHA-256(ASCII(verifier))), bina padding. Token endpoint par client verifier bhejta hai; server dobara SHA-256 karke stored challenge se compare karta hai. Attacker ne agar sirf code aur challenge dekha hai, toh SHA-256 ulta karke verifier nahi nikal sakta.

Length rules RFC 7636 4.1 se: verifier 43 se 128 characters, alphabet [A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~]. 43 characters minimum isliye ki 32 random bytes base64url mein 43 characters bante hain -- yani kam se kam 256 bits entropy ka rasta. Challenge hamesha 43 isliye: SHA-256 output 32 bytes hai, aur 32 bytes ka base64url bina padding 43 characters. Isliye CHALLENGE_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9\-_]{43}$/ -- koi aur length ho toh woh S256 challenge ho hi nahi sakta, aur handleAuthorize use 'not a valid S256 challenge' se reject karta hai.

pkceMatches() pehle VERIFIER_RE se syntax check karta hai (test: 42 chars wala verifier sahi hash ke saath bhi reject), phir safeEqual(s256(verifier), challenge). RFC 7636 appendix B ka example vector units.test.ts mein hai.
why_needed: PKCE ka poora security argument ek one-way hash par tika hai; galat length ya alphabet accept karna weak verifiers ko allow karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Taala aur chaabi ka saancha: aap pehle sirf saancha (challenge) jama karte ho, chaabi (verifier) baad mein laate ho. Saanche se chaabi banana mumkin nahi.
how_it_works: authorize: CHALLENGE_RE test -> transaction mein codeChallenge. token: VERIFIER_RE test -> s256(verifier) -> safeEqual with stored challenge.
in_this_project: src/secrets.ts VERIFIER_RE, CHALLENGE_RE, s256, pkceMatches; src/server.ts handleAuthorize, codeGrant; test/units.test.ts RFC 7636 appendix B vector aur syntax test.
advantages: Malformed challenge /authorize par hi pakda jaata hai
disadvantages: Clients ko RFC ka exact alphabet follow karna padta hai
common_mistakes: base64 (padding ke saath) use karna base64url ki jagah
Verifier syntax check skip karna
Hash ko hex mein compare karna
follow_up_questions: plain method kab safe hota tha?
Verifier ko kahan store karna chahiye SPA mein?

question: state and nonce both look like random values the client sends. What does each one protect against, and how does this server handle them?
answer_hinglish:
state OAuth ka parameter hai aur CSRF on the redirect se bachata hai: client /authorize se pehle random state banata hai, apni session mein rakhta hai, aur callback par jo state aaya usse compare karta hai. Agar attacker apna khud ka code victim ke browser se client ke callback par bhejwaye (login CSRF / code injection), toh state match nahi karega. Server ka kaam bas state ko as-is wapas karna hai -- success redirect par bhi aur error redirect par bhi.

nonce OIDC ka hai aur id_token replay se bachata hai: client nonce bhejta hai, server use id_token ke 'nonce' claim mein daalta hai, aur client check karta hai ki id_token mein wahi nonce hai jo usne is login ke liye bheja tha. Purana ya doosre flow ka id_token inject karne par nonce match nahi hoga.

Is server mein: handleAuthorize state aur nonce ko LoginTransaction mein rakhta hai; handleLogin redirect mein state wapas deta hai; nonce code ke saath store hota hai aur sendTokens id_token mein daalta hai. Refresh par naye id_token mein nonce nahi hota (OIDC Core 12.2). Interop: openid-client wrong state par callback reject karta hai aur wrong expected nonce par id_token reject karta hai -- dono test interop.test.ts mein. Mutation M13 (state drop) ne kai tests red kiye.
why_needed: Dono client-side checks hain; server galti se drop kare ya badle toh client ki protection toot jaati hai.
real_world_analogy: state: restaurant ka token number -- khana wahi lo jiska number tumhara hai. nonce: cake par likha naam -- cake (id_token) usi ke liye bana jisne order kiya.
how_it_works: state: tx.state -> redirectWith(..., { code, state, iss }). nonce: tx.nonce -> code.nonce -> claims.nonce in sendTokens (code grant only).
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleAuthorize, handleLogin, sendTokens; test/login.test.ts state passthrough; test/interop.test.ts wrong state aur wrong nonce tests.
advantages: Server stateless pass-through; validation client karta hai
Error redirects bhi state rakhte hain
disadvantages: Server khud state/nonce enforce nahi karta (optional parameters)
common_mistakes: state ko predictable rakhna
nonce ko refresh id_token mein daal dena
Callback par state check bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: PKCE ke baad state ki zaroorat bachi hai kya?
nonce kab mandatory hai (implicit flow)?

question: Why does the access token have aud = issuer/userinfo and typ at+jwt, while the id_token has aud = client_id and typ JWT? Where does azp come in?
answer_hinglish:
Do tokens, do audiences. id_token client ke liye hai: 'user kaun hai'. Isliye aud = client_id. Access token resource server (API) ke liye hai; stage 1 mein ek hi resource hai -- hamara /userinfo -- isliye default accessTokenAudience = issuer + '/userinfo'. Agar dono ka aud same hota, toh client ka id_token API ko bhej kar access token ki tarah chalaya ja sakta tha, ya ulta.

typ bhi alag hai: RFC 9068 (JWT profile for OAuth access tokens) kehta hai access token ka header typ 'at+jwt' ho. id_token 'JWT' typ ke saath sign hota hai. verifyJwt typ ko exact match karta hai, toh /userinfo par id_token bhejo toh 'unexpected typ' -- aur /logout par access token ko id_token_hint banao toh bhi reject. Mutation M12 (aud check hata do) par id_token-as-access-token test red nahi hua tha kyunki typ check ne pehle hi rok diya -- defence in depth ka seedha saboot.

azp (authorized party) OIDC mein tab chahiye jab id_token ke aud mein kai values hon. Yahan aud hamesha ek string (client_id) hai, toh azp emit nahi hota; openid-client ka validateIdTokenAuthorizedParty single aud ke saath pass karta hai.
why_needed: Token confusion attacks (ek token ko doosri jagah chalana) audience aur type separation se rukte hain.
real_world_analogy: Cinema ticket aur parking ticket dono kaagaz hain, lekin gate wala sirf apna wala maanta hai -- aud aur typ wahi label hain.
how_it_works: sendTokens: access { typ at+jwt, aud: ctx.audience, client_id, scope, jti }, id_token { typ JWT, aud: client.client_id, nonce, at_hash, sid }.
in_this_project: src/server.ts sendTokens, handleUserinfo; src/jwt.ts verifyJwt; test/userinfo.test.ts 'the id_token presented as an access token'.
advantages: Token confusion do jagah se rukta hai (aud + typ)
disadvantages: Sirf ek resource; multi-API audiences (resource indicators, RFC 8707) nahi
common_mistakes: Access token ko identity proof maanna
typ check na karna
aud array mein client aur API dono daal dena
follow_up_questions: Resource indicators (RFC 8707) kya hain?
Agar do APIs hon toh audience kaise chunoge?

question: How is the kid computed as an RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, and why does the exact JSON string matter?
answer_hinglish:
RFC 7638 thumbprint: JWK ke sirf REQUIRED members lo (EC key ke liye crv, kty, x, y), unhe lexicographic order mein rakho, bina whitespace ke JSON banao, aur uska SHA-256 base64url karo. Result ek deterministic id hai: same public key -> hamesha same kid, kisi bhi implementation mein.

jwkThumbprint() yeh string haath se banata hai: {"crv":"P-256","kty":"EC","x":"...","y":"..."}. JSON.stringify par bharosa nahi kiya kyunki object key order aur extra members (kid, use, alg) string badal dete aur thumbprint galat ho jaata. Ek byte bhi alag = alag hash.

Fayde is project mein: (1) discovery.test.ts har published key ka kid thumbprint se recompute karke match karta hai. (2) FileKeyRing.open keys.json ke stored kid ko PEM se nikle kid se compare karta hai; mismatch par 'does not match its key' aur start fail -- hand-edited ya corrupt file pakdi jaati hai (keys.test.ts). (3) Do processes ya restarts mein same key ka same kid. Note: kid sirf lookup ke liye hai, security signature se aati hai -- isliye 'a token signed by a different key with the same kid' test bhi hai jo signature check se fail hota hai.
why_needed: kid se verifier key chunta hai; non-deterministic kid rotation aur caching ko confuse karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Fingerprint: insaan ka naam badal sakta hai, fingerprint nahi. Thumbprint key ka fingerprint hai.
how_it_works: publicKey.export({format:'jwk'}) -> {crv,kty,x,y} -> canonical string -> sha256 -> base64url.
in_this_project: src/jwt.ts jwkThumbprint, signingKeyFromPrivate; src/keys.ts FileKeyRing.open kid check; test/discovery.test.ts; test/keys.test.ts.
disadvantages: Sirf EC keys ke liye likha hai (RSA ke members alag)
common_mistakes: JSON.stringify(jwk) ka hash lena
kid ko trust ka source maanna
follow_up_questions: RSA key ka thumbprint kaunse members se banta hai?
kid collision ho toh verifier kya kare?

question: What exactly does RFC 7009 revocation do in this server: which tokens, which status codes, and why is an unknown or foreign token answered with 200?
answer_hinglish:
/revoke client authenticate karta hai (confidential: Basic, public: client_id), phir 'token' parameter leta hai. Sirf refresh tokens revoke hote hain: getRefresh(sha256(token)) mila aur woh isi client ka hai toh uski poori family revoke -- RFC 7009 2.1 kehta hai server SHOULD same grant ke access tokens bhi invalidate kare, aur family revoke se hamare /userinfo par access tokens bhi 401 ho jaate hain.

200 ke cases: token unknown (RFC kehta hai invalid token par bhi 200, kyunki client ka maqsad -- token kaam na kare -- pura ho gaya), access token bheja (lookup refresh store mein hai, kuch nahi milta, 200), aur doosre client ka token. Aakhri case par RFC 'refused' kehta hai; maine chuna ki 200 do aur kuch mat karo, taaki endpoint yeh na bataye ki kaunsa token exist karta hai. README mein yeh decision likha hai. token_type_hint ko server padhta hi nahi -- woh optional optimisation hai.

Errors: client auth fail -> 401 invalid_client + WWW-Authenticate; token missing -> 400 invalid_request; non-form body -> 400. Tests revoke.test.ts mein; mutation M15 (ownership ignore) 'another client cannot revoke my token' ne pakdi.
why_needed: Logout ya app uninstall par client ko apne tokens khatam karne ka standard rasta chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Lost credit card report karna: bank card band karta hai; galat number bhi report karo toh 'theek hai' bolta hai, aur doosre ka card aap band nahi kar sakte.
how_it_works: authenticateClient -> token -> getRefresh(hash) -> rt.clientId === client -> revokeFamily -> 200 empty body, no-store.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleRevoke; test/revoke.test.ts; test/flow.test.ts revoke step.
advantages: Family revoke se access tokens bhi (userinfo par)
disadvantages: Access token ko seedha revoke nahi kar sakte
Foreign token par 'refused' nahi -- RFC se thoda alag
common_mistakes: Unknown token par 400 dena
Kisi bhi client ko kisi ka token revoke karne dena
follow_up_questions: Access token revocation ke liye jti deny-list kaise banaoge?
Introspection aur revocation mein kya fark hai?

question: List concrete redirect_uri matching attacks and show which line of this server stops each one.
answer_hinglish:
Attacks: (1) Prefix: registered 'https://app/callback', attacker bhejta hai 'https://app/callback.evil.test' ya '/callback/../attacker-path'. (2) Subdomain / host: 'https://evil.app.example.test/callback'. (3) Extra query ya trailing slash: kuch servers inhe 'same' maan lete hain, aur open redirect wale page par code pahunch jaata hai. (4) Port: loopback par doosra port (dusra local process). (5) Case: host case-insensitive hai par path nahi; normalisation bugs. (6) Doosre client ka registered URI apne client_id ke saath. (7) Fragment: '#' ke baad ka hissa browser rakhta hai, scripts padh sakti hain.

Defence: redirectUriAllowed() = client.redirect_uris.includes(redirectUri) -- exact string, koi normalisation, wildcard ya prefix nahi. Yeh sab ek line se rukte hain; authorize.test.ts 8 variants (prefix, trailing slash, extra query, other port, case, host, other client's URI, missing) chalata hai. Mismatch par redirect hi nahi: 400 HTML page, koi Set-Cookie nahi. Config time par checkRedirectUri: absolute URL, koi fragment nahi, http sirf loopback (127.0.0.1, [::1], localhost). Token endpoint par redirect_uri dobara compare hota hai (code ke saath stored wala). Mutation M1 (prefix match) teen tests red karti hai. Logout ka post_logout_redirect_uri bhi isi rule par hai.
why_needed: Redirect URI hi woh jagah hai jahan code jaata hai; matching bug = code theft.
real_world_analogy: Courier sirf likhe hue exact address par deliver karta hai; 'same building' ya 'milta-julta naam' nahi.
how_it_works: authorize: findClient -> redirectUriAllowed (exact) -> warna errorPage 400. token: c.redirectUri !== redirectUri -> invalid_grant.
in_this_project: src/server.ts redirectUriAllowed, handleAuthorize, codeGrant; src/config.ts checkRedirectUri; test/authorize.test.ts.
advantages: Ek simple rule, saare variants cover
disadvantages: RFC 8252 loopback ka 'any port' rule support nahi; native apps ko har port register karna padega
common_mistakes: Regex ya startsWith se match
Mismatch par error ke saath redirect kar dena
Token endpoint par redirect_uri check skip
follow_up_questions: Native apps ke dynamic loopback ports kaise handle karoge?
Open redirector client ke andar ho toh exact match bhi kya bacha paata hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Exact match strict hai aur kabhi kabhi developer-unfriendly, lekin har relaxation ek naya attack surface hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Client ke registered callback page par khud open redirect hai: exact match pass, lekin code aage leak -- PKCE aur client binding tab bhi bachate hain.
advanced.alternatives: RFC 8252 loopback port flexibility sirf loopback ke liye; PAR (RFC 9126) jahan redirect_uri back channel par jaata hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Matching O(n) per client list; scale issue nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Registration time par URI review, PAR, monitoring of rejected redirect_uri attempts.

question: What is an OAuth mix-up attack, and how does the iss parameter in the authorization response (RFC 9207) help? What does this server do?
answer_hinglish:
Mix-up tab hota hai jab ek client kai authorization servers (AS) ke saath kaam karta hai, jinme se ek attacker ka hai. Attacker client ko confuse karta hai ki response kis AS se aaya: client ek honest AS ka code attacker ke AS ke token endpoint par bhej deta hai (code leak), ya ulta. Root cause: authorization response mein yeh nahi likha ki kisne bheja.

RFC 9207 fix: AS har authorization response (success aur error dono) mein 'iss' parameter daale, aur client check kare ki yeh wahi issuer hai jise usne request bheji thi. Is server mein handleLogin success redirect mein code, state aur iss = ctx.issuer bhejta hai; handleAuthorize ke error redirects (fail()) bhi iss bhejte hain. Discovery mein authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true hai, toh openid-client iss ko expect aur validate karta hai -- interop flow tests isse cover karte hain (openid-client authorizationCodeGrant iss check karta hai).

Yeh sirf hamare honest side ka kaam hai; asli check client karta hai. PKCE bhi madad karta hai kyunki attacker ke paas verifier nahi, lekin RFC 9700 dono recommend karta hai.
why_needed: Multi-provider clients (Google + company IdP) aam hain; bina iss ke client ko pata nahi response kis AS ka hai.
real_world_analogy: Do banks ke cheque ek jaise dikhte hain; bank ka naam cheque par chhapa na ho toh aap galat bank mein jama kar doge.
how_it_works: redirectWith(res, tx.redirectUri, { code, state: tx.state, iss: ctx.issuer }); error path bhi iss ke saath.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleLogin, handleAuthorize (fail), discoveryDocument; test/flow.test.ts iss check; test/interop.test.ts.
disadvantages: Sirf tab kaam ka jab client check kare
common_mistakes: Sirf success par iss bhejna
Discovery mein advertise na karna (client check skip kar deta hai)
follow_up_questions: Per-AS redirect_uri bhi mix-up kaise rokta hai?
JARM kya hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ek extra parameter vs client-side complexity; trade-off clearly worth it.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Client iss ignore kare toh protection zero; purane clients jo unknown params reject karein (rare).
advanced.alternatives: Per-issuer redirect URIs, JARM (signed responses), PAR.
advanced.production_improvements: Client SDKs mein iss check default on; logs mein iss mismatch alerts.

question: What is authorization code injection, and which combination of checks in codeGrant defeats it?
answer_hinglish:
Code injection: attacker kisi victim ka code (leak hua, ya apna khud ka) client ke callback mein inject karta hai taaki client use redeem kare aur galat account se bandh jaaye, ya attacker victim ka code apne client session mein daalta hai. Bina extra binding ke, code sirf 'bearer' hai.

codeGrant ki layers: (1) code ka hash consume() -- missing ya reused toh invalid_grant, reused par family revoke. (2) expiresAt (60 s). (3) c.clientId === authenticated client -- doosre client ke liye bana code kaam nahi karta. (4) c.redirectUri === request ka redirect_uri. (5) pkceMatches(verifier, c.codeChallenge) -- yeh asli injection defence hai: injected code us flow ka hai jiska verifier attacker/victim ke paas hai, injecting session ke paas nahi, toh PKCE fail. (6) User abhi bhi exist karta hai.

Important order detail: consume() sabse pehle hota hai, toh code pehli presentation par burn -- galat verifier ke saath bhi. Matlab attacker ka galat guess code ko legit client ke liye bhi khatam kar deta hai (fail-closed), aur agar legit client pehle redeem kar chuka tha toh attacker ka attempt family revoke karta hai. Mutations M3 (PKCE skip) aur M4/M5 tests ne pakdi.
why_needed: PKCE sirf 'public client ka secret' nahi hai; woh code ko us browser session se bandhta hai jisne flow shuru kiya.
real_world_analogy: Kisi aur ka luggage tag apne bag par lagana: airline tag ke saath boarding pass ka number bhi match karti hai (PKCE).
how_it_works: consume -> expiry -> client -> redirect_uri -> PKCE -> user -> family + tokens.
in_this_project: src/server.ts codeGrant; test/token.test.ts PKCE, other client, redirect_uri, burned code tests.
disadvantages: Attacker legit user ka code burn karke DoS kar sakta hai (jo code leak hua ho)
common_mistakes: PKCE ko confidential clients ke liye optional rakhna
Checks ke baad consume karna (race window)
follow_up_questions: Code burn-on-failure ka DoS risk kitna hai?
nonce code injection mein kya role play karta hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Burn-first se replay safety milti hai, cost: leaked code ka galat use legit login todta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Code browser history/logs se leak; attacker race mein pehle pahunche -- PKCE ke bina woh jeet jaata.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Har code ek atomic update; scale par DB index on code_hash.
advanced.production_improvements: Failed PKCE attempts ka monitoring; client ko clear error.

question: What is login CSRF on an authorization server's login form, and how do the synchronizer token and the transaction cookie stop it here?
answer_hinglish:
Login CSRF: attacker apni site par ek hidden form banata hai jo victim ke browser se hamare /login par attacker ke username/password POST karta hai. Victim bina jaane attacker ke account mein login ho jaata hai, aur client app mein jo data daalega (card, documents) woh attacker ke account mein jaayega. Ya attacker kisi aur ke transaction ko complete karwa deta hai.

Defence: /authorize par server ek LoginTransaction banata hai jisme random csrfToken hai, aur transaction id HttpOnly cookie auth_tx mein jaata hai (Path=/login, SameSite=Lax). Login page ke form mein hidden csrf_token. handleLogin cookie se transaction nikalta hai aur safeEqual(form token, tx.csrfToken) karta hai. Attacker ki site cookie bhej bhi de (SameSite Lax cross-site POST par cookie nahi bhejta, extra layer), woh csrf_token nahi padh sakta (same-origin policy), toh 403.

Tests login.test.ts: bad token 403, missing token 403, DOOSRE transaction ka token 403 (token transaction se bandha hai, global nahi), missing cookie 400. Mutation M9 (CSRF check hata do) teen tests red karti hai. Transaction single-use hai aur 10 minute mein expire.
why_needed: Authorization server ka login page sabse valuable target hai; wahan CSRF se account confusion hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank ka form jisme ek serial number chhapa hai jo sirf counter par mila tha; ghar se bana form uske bina reject.
how_it_works: authorize: tx {id, csrfToken} save, Set-Cookie auth_tx=id. login: cookie -> tx -> expiry -> safeEqual(csrf) -> password.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleAuthorize, txCookie, handleLogin; src/pages.ts loginPage; test/login.test.ts.
disadvantages: Server-side state per login attempt
common_mistakes: Sirf SameSite par bharosa
Global CSRF token jo kisi bhi transaction ke saath chale
Token ko non-constant-time compare
follow_up_questions: Double-submit cookie pattern kya hai aur yahan kyun nahi?
SameSite=Strict yahan kya todta?

question: Where does this server need constant-time comparison, and where is it NOT needed because of how secrets are looked up?
answer_hinglish:
Timing attack: agar compare pehle mismatching byte par ruk jaaye, toh response time se attacker byte-by-byte secret guess kar sakta hai. Isliye jahan bhi server ek attacker-supplied value ko stored secret se COMPARE karta hai, constant-time chahiye.

Yahan: CSRF token (safeEqual), PKCE (safeEqual(s256(verifier), challenge)), scrypt output (timingSafeEqual inside verifySecret). safeEqual dono sides ko pehle SHA-256 karta hai -- isse length ka fark bhi chhup jaata hai (timingSafeEqual alag length par throw karta hai) aur compare hamesha 32 bytes ka.

Jahan zaroorat NAHI: authorization codes, refresh tokens, session cookies. Inhe compare kiya hi nahi jaata -- server unka sha256 nikal kar Map lookup karta hai (getRefresh(sha256(token))). Attacker ke paas hash ka control nahi, aur 256-bit random token ke hash ko timing se guess karna practical nahi. Same pattern database index lookup ke saath bhi safe hai. Unknown user par bhi dummy scrypt chalta hai taaki 'user exist nahi karta' fast response se leak na ho. Honest note: units.test.ts sirf correctness test karta hai, timing measure nahi kiya.
why_needed: Crypto sahi ho lekin compare galat ho toh secret leak ho sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Tijori ka taala jo har galat number par turant 'click' kare -- chor sun ke number nikal lega.
how_it_works: safeEqual(a,b): sha256(a), sha256(b), timingSafeEqual. Lookups: sha256(secret) -> Map.get.
in_this_project: src/secrets.ts safeEqual, verifySecret, verifyAgainstDummy; src/store.ts (maps keyed by hash).
advantages: Hash lookup se compare ki zaroorat hi khatam
disadvantages: Timing kabhi measure nahi kiya
common_mistakes: === se secret compare
Length pehle check karke early return
Unknown user par turant return
follow_up_questions: Network jitter ke bawajood timing attacks kaise kaam karte hain?
HMAC compare kab chahiye?

question: Explain the scrypt parameters N, r and p used here, the maxmem setting, and why parseSecretHash puts bounds on them.
answer_hinglish:
scrypt memory-hard password hash hai. N = CPU/memory cost (power of 2), r = block size, p = parallelism. Memory roughly 128 * N * r bytes: N=2^17, r=8 par lagbhag 128 MiB per hash. Yeh OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet ka minimum hai aur DEFAULT_SCRYPT yahi hai. Memory-hard hona GPU/ASIC attackers ke liye mehenga banata hai.

Node ka scrypt default maxmem 32 MiB hai, toh N=2^17 fail ho jaata; isliye scrypt() helper maxmem = 128*N*r + 16 MiB set karta hai. Hash format 'scrypt$N$r$p$salt$hash' parameters ko hash ke saath rakhta hai, toh cost badalne par purane hashes verify hote rehte hain, aur tests N=2^14 use karte hain (fast) jabki code path same hai.

Bounds kyun? Config file se aaya hash parameters decide karta hai. Hostile ya galat config N=2^30 maang ke har login par gigabytes allocate karwa sakta tha (DoS). parseSecretHash N ko 2^10..2^20 aur power of two, r 1..32, p 1..16, salt >= 8 bytes, key exactly 32 bytes tak rakhta hai -- units.test.ts 'rejects malformed hashes and absurd parameters'. Kitna time per login lagta hai yeh measure nahi kiya (PLAN stage 5).
why_needed: Password DB leak hone par slow, memory-hard hash hi offline cracking ko mehenga banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Tijori jisme har baar kholne ke liye ek bhaari pahiya ghumana padta hai: aapke liye ek baar theek, chor ke liye karodon baar namumkin.
how_it_works: hashSecret: random 16-byte salt -> scrypt(N,r,p,maxmem) -> format string. verifySecret: parse (bounds) -> scrypt -> timingSafeEqual.
in_this_project: src/secrets.ts DEFAULT_SCRYPT, hashSecret, parseSecretHash, verifySecret; src/hash-secret.ts CLI; test/units.test.ts.
advantages: Parameters hash ke saath, upgrade aasaan
disadvantages: Har login par bhaari memory; concurrency par libuv thread pool limit
Cost measure nahi kiya
common_mistakes: Default maxmem par production cost chalana (fail)
Parameters global config mein rakhna, hash mein nahi
follow_up_questions: argon2id kyun aaj zyada recommend hota hai?
Login par rehash-on-verify kaise karoge?

question: Which HTTP security headers does the login page send and what does each one prevent? Why is there no form-action directive?
answer_hinglish:
sendHtml() har HTML response par yeh headers lagata hai: (1) Content-Security-Policy: "default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; frame-ancestors 'none'" -- page koi script, image ya external resource load nahi kar sakta (XSS ka asar kam), aur frame-ancestors 'none' kehta hai koi site is page ko iframe mein nahi rakh sakti (clickjacking: attacker invisible iframe mein hamara login form rakh ke user se click karwata hai). (2) X-Frame-Options: DENY -- wahi cheez purane browsers ke liye. (3) Referrer-Policy: no-referrer -- URL (jisme query params ho sakte hain) doosri sites ko Referer header mein nahi jaata. (4) Cache-Control: no-store + Pragma: no-cache -- login page aur error pages cache mein nahi.

form-action kyun nahi? Kuch browsers form-action ko form submit ke BAAD wale redirect par bhi apply karte hain. Hamara /login POST 302 se client ke redirect_uri par bhejta hai -- form-action 'self' us redirect ko block kar deta. Comment http.ts mein yahi kehta hai. Saath mein har dynamic value escapeHtml se jaati hai (units.test.ts). Honest gap: real browser mein framing test nahi kiya (PLAN stage 4).
why_needed: Login page phishing aur clickjacking ka target hai; headers sasta defence hain.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan ke counter par sheesha: grahak dekh sakta hai, lekin koi aur counter ke upar apna parda nahi daal sakta.
how_it_works: sendHtml -> noStore -> writeHead with CSP, XFO, Referrer-Policy.
in_this_project: src/http.ts sendHtml, escapeHtml; test/authorize.test.ts headers check; test/units.test.ts escape test.
advantages: Har HTML response par ek hi jagah se
disadvantages: Real browser test nahi
common_mistakes: form-action 'self' lagake OAuth redirect tod dena
Sirf X-Frame-Options, CSP nahi
follow_up_questions: Clickjacking demo kaise banaoge?
HSTS yahan kyun nahi set hai (http loopback)?

question: In refreshGrant, why is the scope check placed BEFORE the atomic markUsed, and what other ordering decisions matter there?
answer_hinglish:
refreshGrant ka order: token hash lookup -> client match -> family exists aur revoked nahi -> expiry -> rt.used fast path (reuse) -> scope narrowing check -> user exists -> markUsed (atomic) -> sendTokens.

Scope check markUsed se pehle kyun: agar client galti se zyada scope maange (invalid_scope), toh request reject hoti hai -- lekin token burn nahi hona chahiye. Agar markUsed pehle hota, toh ek galat request client ka valid refresh token khatam kar deti aur agla sahi refresh 'reuse' lagta -> family revoke -> user logout. Test 'scope can be narrowed but not widened; a refused scope request does not burn the token' yahi check karta hai.

Doosre decisions: (1) Client mismatch par family revoke NAHI -- doosra client kisi ka token bhej ke uski family nahi maar sakta. (2) Revoked family check reuse check se pehle -- revoked family ka token simply 'revoked'. (3) rt.used sirf fast path hai; asli decision markUsed karta hai (database mein do concurrent requests dono fast path paar kar sakti hain). (4) Narrowed scope sirf is response ke liye; family original scope rakhti hai, toh agla refresh full scope de sakta hai (RFC 6749 6). Saare validations side effect se pehle -- general rule.
why_needed: Order of checks security code mein behaviour hai; galat order DoS ya bypass banata hai.
real_world_analogy: ATM pehle PIN aur amount check karta hai, phir card se paise kaatta hai -- ulta nahi.
how_it_works: Validation (read-only) -> one atomic write (markUsed) -> issue new tokens.
in_this_project: src/server.ts refreshGrant, reuseDetected; test/refresh.test.ts.
advantages: Galat requests legit tokens nahi todti
disadvantages: Order fragile hai; refactor mein tootna aasaan (tests hi bachate hain)
common_mistakes: Pehle burn phir validate
Client mismatch par family revoke
follow_up_questions: Concurrent requests mein fast path aur markUsed ka rishta?
Scope narrowing ko family mein persist karna chahiye kya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Validate-then-commit pattern simple hai; har naya check commit se pehle hona chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Database store mein network failure markUsed ke baad aur response se pehle: token burned, client ke paas naya nahi -> retry = reuse -> family revoke.
advanced.alternatives: Grace window (previous token ek baar aur kuch second), ya idempotency key per refresh.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Har refresh ek row update; hot rows nahi kyunki har token alag.
advanced.production_improvements: Reuse events ka audit log aur alert; false positive rate monitor.

question: A refresh token is presented by a DIFFERENT client than the one it was issued to. Why does the server answer invalid_grant but NOT revoke the family?
answer_hinglish:
Reuse detection family isliye revoke karti hai kyunki reuse chori ka signal hai aur server nahi jaanta kaun attacker hai. Lekin galat client ka case alag hai: request authenticated client X ki hai aur token client Y ka. Agar is par Y ki family revoke ho jaati, toh koi bhi client (public client bina secret ke bhi, bas client_id) kisi aur ka token bhej ke victim ki session khatam kar sakta -- ek sasta DoS, aur ulta attacker ko ek 'kill switch' de deta.

Isliye refreshGrant mein client check family lookup se pehle aata hai aur sirf invalid_grant 'issued to another client' deta hai. Token Y ke liye valid rehta hai. Test 'a refresh token of another client -> invalid_grant and the family is NOT revoked' pehle other-spa se bhejta hai, phir spa se refresh 200 expect karta hai.

Same soch /revoke mein: doosre client ka token 200 aur kuch nahi hota. Code reuse alag hai: wahan same code dobara aaya, jo leak ka seedha saboot hai, toh revoke. Rule: revoke tab karo jab signal ho ki LEGIT holder ka secret compromise hua; jab sirf koi galat request kare, tab nahi.
why_needed: Security response khud ek attack vector na bane.
real_world_analogy: Kisi aur ka ATM card aapke account se nahi chalega; bank us card ko block bhi nahi karta sirf isliye ki aapne try kiya.
how_it_works: getRefresh -> rt.clientId !== client.client_id -> invalid_grant (no side effect).
in_this_project: src/server.ts refreshGrant, handleRevoke; test/refresh.test.ts; test/revoke.test.ts.
disadvantages: Attacker jisne token chura liya aur galat client se try kiya, uska signal ignore hota hai
common_mistakes: Har anomaly par revoke kar dena
Client check family revoke ke baad rakhna
follow_up_questions: Kya is event ko log/alert karna chahiye?
Public client ka client_id public hai -- isse kya farak padta hai?

question: Two browser tabs of the same SPA refresh at the same moment with the same refresh token. What happens in this server, and what should the client do?
answer_hinglish:
Dono requests same token hash ke saath aati hain. Ek request markUsed jeetegi (in-memory aur file store dono mein yeh synchronous check-and-set hai) aur naya refresh token + access token paayegi. Doosri ya toh rt.used fast path par ya markUsed false par reuseDetected() mein jaayegi -> poori family revoke -> invalid_grant 'refresh token reuse detected'. Ab jeetne wale tab ka naya refresh token bhi dead hai (same family), aur /userinfo par access tokens 401. User effectively logout.

Yeh design ka conscious trade-off hai: server legit concurrency aur chori mein fark nahi kar sakta, aur fail-safe direction chuna. Koi grace period nahi hai -- README aur AUTH-005 ke advanced section mein likha hai.

Client side fix: refresh ko serialize karo -- ek hi tab/worker refresh kare (BroadcastChannel ya Web Lock ke saath), baaki naye token ka wait karein. Ya refresh token ko service worker / backend-for-frontend mein rakho. Server side alternatives (abhi nahi bane): chhota grace window jisme previous token ek baar aur same naya token de, ya idempotency. Debug signal: logs mein error_description 'reuse detected' dikhe aur user complain kare 'har kuch der mein logout' -- concurrency pehla shak.
why_needed: Rotation ka sabse common production complaint false-positive reuse hai.
real_world_analogy: Do log ek hi coupon ek saath counter par dete hain: dukaan maan leti hai ki coupon copy hua aur dono ka account freeze.
how_it_works: Request A: markUsed true -> new tokens. Request B: markUsed false -> revokeFamily -> invalid_grant. A ke tokens bhi revoked family mein.
in_this_project: src/server.ts refreshGrant, reuseDetected; src/store.ts markUsed; test/refresh.test.ts reuse test.
disadvantages: Legit concurrency user ko logout karti hai
common_mistakes: Har tab mein alag-alag refresh logic
Response kho jaane par purana token retry karna
follow_up_questions: Grace window kaise implement karoge bina security tode?
BFF pattern isme kaise madad karta hai?

question: Read refreshGrant line by line: what error does a client get for (a) an unknown token, (b) a revoked family, (c) an expired token, (d) a reused token? Why does the order matter for debugging?
answer_hinglish:
refreshGrant har failure ke liye invalid_grant deta hai (RFC 6749 5.2), lekin error_description alag hai -- debugging ke liye yahi signal hai. (a) Unknown: getRefresh(sha256(token)) undefined -> 'refresh token is invalid'. (b) Client mismatch -> 'issued to another client'. (c) Family missing ya revoked -> 'refresh token is revoked'. (d) Expired -> 'refresh token expired'. (e) Already used -> reuseDetected -> family revoke + 'refresh token reuse detected; the token family is revoked'. (f) Scope zyada -> invalid_scope. (g) User config se hata diya -> 'user no longer exists'.

Order matter karta hai: revoked check expiry aur reuse se pehle hai. Toh ek baar family revoke ho gayi (reuse, logout, /revoke, code reuse), uske baad koi bhi token -- purana ya naya -- 'revoked' dikhayega, 'reuse' nahi. Debug karte waqt: agar description 'revoked' hai toh poochho family kis wajah se mari -- pehle ka reuse event, logout, ya revoke call. Agar 'reuse detected' hai toh yahi request ne family maari. Note: expired check used check se pehle hai, toh expired-and-used token 'expired' dikhayega aur family revoke nahi hogi. Tests refresh.test.ts mein har case ka hai.
why_needed: Same error code, alag reasons: description aur check order se root cause milta hai.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ka checklist order: pehle pulse (zinda hai?), phir baaki tests -- order se diagnosis badalta hai.
how_it_works: Sequential early returns, side effect sirf reuseDetected aur markUsed par.
in_this_project: src/server.ts refreshGrant; test/refresh.test.ts.
advantages: Clear descriptions, ek hi error code (spec compliant)
disadvantages: Description attacker ko bhi hint deta hai (token exist karta hai ya nahi)
common_mistakes: Har case ka alag error code invent karna
Logs mein raw token print karna
follow_up_questions: error_description mein kitni detail dena safe hai?
Expired-and-used par revoke karna chahiye kya?

question: An authorization code is burned on its first presentation even if that request fails PKCE, but NOT if client authentication fails. Why this split?
answer_hinglish:
handleToken pehle form parse karta hai, phir authenticateClient. Agar client auth fail (galat secret, galat Basic header) toh request codeGrant tak pahunchti hi nahi -- code store ko chhua nahi jaata. Matlab koi bhi random request jo client hone ka saboot nahi deti, codes burn nahi kar sakti; warna ek unauthenticated attacker leaked code ko sirf bhej ke legit client ka login tod deta.

Client auth pass hone ke baad codeGrant sabse pehle consume() karta hai. Ab code burned hai, chahe aage expiry, client mismatch, redirect_uri ya PKCE fail ho. Kyun? (1) Replay safety: ek code ek hi baar 'try' hota hai, toh verifier brute force ka sawaal hi nahi. (2) Atomicity simple: ek atomic consume, phir read-only checks. (3) Fail-closed: shak ki situation mein code khatam.

Trade-off: public client ka 'auth' sirf client_id hai (koi secret nahi), toh public client ke case mein koi bhi jo code aur client_id jaanta hai woh code burn kar sakta hai. Leaked code ka nuksan: ek login fail -- data leak nahi. Tests: token.test.ts 'the code is burned by its first presentation, even a failed one'; README design notes mein dono halves likhe hain.
why_needed: Kab state badalni hai, yeh security decision hai, implementation detail nahi.
real_world_analogy: Exam hall: pehle ID card check (bina ID andar hi nahi), andar aane ke baad question paper ek hi baar milta hai, chahe pehla jawab galat ho.
how_it_works: handleToken: readOAuthForm -> authenticateClient (no store access) -> grant routing -> codeGrant: consume first.
in_this_project: src/server.ts handleToken, authenticateClient, codeGrant; test/token.test.ts.
advantages: Unauthenticated requests ka koi side effect nahi
disadvantages: Public clients ke liye burn-by-anyone
common_mistakes: Validation ke baad consume (race)
Client auth se pehle code lookup
follow_up_questions: Confidential vs public client ke liye alag rule hona chahiye?
Burn events ko monitor karoge?

question: Which HTTP status codes and error formats does this server use for OAuth errors, and when does a 401 carry a WWW-Authenticate header?
answer_hinglish:
OAuth errors JSON hote hain: { error, error_description } (RFC 6749 5.2), aur oauthError() hamesha no-store lagata hai. Status codes: 400 invalid_request (missing ya repeated parameter, galat content-type), 400 invalid_grant (code/refresh token problems), 400 invalid_scope, unsupported_grant_type, unauthorized_client; 401 invalid_client (client auth fail) -- yahan WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="token" bhi jaata hai kyunki 401 ke saath challenge dena HTTP ka rule hai aur RFC 6749 isse maangta hai jab client ne Authorization header use kiya; 405 galat method (Allow header ke saath); 413 body 16 KiB se badi; 404 unknown path; 500 server_error (unexpected exception, detail leak nahi).

/userinfo Bearer errors RFC 6750 style: 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", aur 403 insufficient_scope jab token mein openid nahi.

Browser-facing endpoints (/authorize errors jahan redirect nahi ho sakta, /login, /logout) JSON nahi, HTML error page dete hain -- user ko dikhana hai. /authorize ke redirectable errors client ke redirect_uri par query params (error, error_description, state, iss) se jaate hain. Tests token.test.ts expectOAuthError har error par no-store bhi check karta hai.
why_needed: Clients standard error codes par logic banate hain; galat format interop todta hai.
real_world_analogy: Hospital ke reception ka standard form: har problem ka ek code aur ek line explanation.
how_it_works: oauthError(res, status, error, description, headers) -> noStore + sendJson. HttpError (413) -> invalid_request.
in_this_project: src/http.ts oauthError, readBody, MAX_BODY_BYTES; src/server.ts BASIC_CHALLENGE, bearerError, route; test/token.test.ts.
disadvantages: error_description English mein, localisation nahi
common_mistakes: 401 bina WWW-Authenticate
Stack trace response mein bhejna
Browser errors ko JSON mein dena
follow_up_questions: 400 vs 401 invalid_client kab?
RFC 6750 error codes kaunse hain?

question: Why must every token endpoint response carry Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache, including error responses?
answer_hinglish:
Token response mein access token, refresh token aur id_token hote hain -- yeh secrets hain. Agar koi proxy, CDN ya browser cache response ko store kar le, toh agla user ya koi jo cache padh sake woh tokens le sakta hai. RFC 6749 5.1 kehta hai token endpoint MUST Cache-Control: no-store aur Pragma: no-cache (HTTP/1.0 caches ke liye) bheje.

Error responses par bhi kyun? Consistency aur safety: errors mein bhi kabhi-kabhi user-specific info hoti hai, aur ek cached error response legit client ko baar baar galat error de sakta hai. Is server mein noStore() helper hai; oauthError() hamesha usse bulata hai, sendTokens() success par, sendHtml() har HTML page par, aur /userinfo aur /revoke bhi.

Tests: flow.test.ts success response par dono headers check karta hai, aur token.test.ts ka expectOAuthError har error test mein check karta hai. Mutation M14 (success responses se no-store hata do) flow test ko red karti hai. Discovery aur JWKS ulte: woh public hain aur 'public, max-age=300' se cache hote hain -- jaan-boojh ke, taaki clients baar baar fetch na karein.
why_needed: Secrets ko caches mein pahunchne se rokna sabse sasta protection hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank statement ki photocopy shop par chhod dena: ek header kehta hai 'copy mat rakhna'.
how_it_works: noStore(res): setHeader Cache-Control no-store, Pragma no-cache.
in_this_project: src/http.ts noStore, oauthError; src/server.ts sendTokens; test/flow.test.ts; test/token.test.ts.
disadvantages: Kuch nahi -- yeh mandatory hai
common_mistakes: Sirf success par lagana
JWKS ko bhi no-store karna (clients ka load badhta)
follow_up_questions: Pragma ab kyun bheja jaata hai?
Discovery ko cache karna safe kyun hai?

question: Why does the server record jti -> token family for every access token, and what does that buy compared with a pure stateless JWT design?
answer_hinglish:
Pure stateless JWT: verifier sirf signature, iss, aud, exp dekhta hai; server ke paas koi record nahi. Fast aur scalable, lekin revocation nahi -- token exp tak chalega chahe family revoke ho gayi ho.

Is server ka hybrid: sendTokens har access token ka random jti banata hai aur recordAccessToken(jti, familyId, expiresAt) se store karta hai. Hamara /userinfo verifyJwt ke baad familyOfAccessToken(jti) -> getFamily -> revoked? check karta hai. Toh code reuse, refresh reuse, /revoke ya logout ke baad hamare apne resource par access token turant 401. Yeh tests mein bahut jagah dikhta hai (refresh reuse ke baad userinfo 401, logout ke baad 401).

Limit: koi third-party API jo token offline verify kare, use yeh record nahi dikhta -- usko token exp (300 s) tak valid lagega. Isliye access token chhota rakha. Stage 2 mein expiresAt record ke saath store hota hai taaki file store compaction expired jti records hata sake. Agla step: introspection (RFC 7662) taaki doosre resource servers bhi revocation dekh sakein -- PLAN mein hai, bana nahi.
why_needed: Revocation chahiye ya scale -- yeh classic JWT trade-off hai; yahan dono ka thoda hissa.
real_world_analogy: Concert band: gate par sirf hologram check (offline), lekin VIP lounge (userinfo) list bhi check karta hai ki band cancel toh nahi hua.
how_it_works: sendTokens: jti random -> recordAccessToken. handleUserinfo: verify -> jti -> family -> revoked? 401.
in_this_project: src/server.ts sendTokens, handleUserinfo; src/store.ts TokenStore.recordAccessToken; src/file-store.ts snapshot (access records ka expiry).
disadvantages: Har token par ek write
Third parties ke liye revocation delay
common_mistakes: Har access token ke liye DB lookup aur phir bhi stateless kehna
jti ko predictable banana
follow_up_questions: Introspection vs deny-list kab?
Access token lifetime kaise choose karoge?

question: What does an fsync per store change cost, which requests pay it most, and how would you measure it honestly?
answer_hinglish:
fsyncSync tab tak return nahi karta jab tak OS ne data disk tak pahuncha nahi diya. Yeh disk aur filesystem par nirbhar hai -- SSD par fast, network disk par slow. Aur kyunki yeh sync call hai, us dauraan Node ka event loop block hai: koi doosri request process nahi hoti.

Kaunse requests zyada pay karte hain: login (session.save + code.save = 2 commits), code grant (code.used, family.create, code.family, access.record, refresh.save = 5 commits, har ek apna fsync), refresh (refresh.used, access.record, refresh.save = 3), logout (har session delete aur har family revoke). /authorize kuch nahi likhta (transactions memory mein), /userinfo sirf padhta hai. Isliye README 'one fsync per request (today one per record)' ko not-implemented list mein rakhta hai.

Is project mein kuch measure nahi hua -- koi number claim nahi. Measure karne ka honest tarika: ek machine par fsync: true aur fsync: false (openFileStores option) dono ke saath token endpoint ka latency distribution, raw results save karo, machine aur disk type likho; alag se ek micro-benchmark sirf writeSync+fsyncSync ka. Phir ek commit per request (records batch) ka fayda dikh sakta hai.
why_needed: Durability ka cost latency mein aata hai; bina measure kiye na 'fast' bolo na 'slow'.
real_world_analogy: Har entry ke baad register ko tijori mein lock karna: safe, lekin har customer ka wait badhta hai.
how_it_works: commit -> durable(writeSync + fsyncSync) -> apply. fsync option tests mein false ho sakta hai.
in_this_project: src/file-store.ts openFileStores (fsync option), commit; README NOT implemented; PLAN stage 5.
disadvantages: Sync fsync event loop block karta hai
Batching nahi
common_mistakes: Benchmark ke bina number quote karna
Production mein fsync off karke durability claim karna
follow_up_questions: Group commit kaise design karoge?
fdatasync vs fsync?

question: Why does the file store use one apply() function both for live changes and for replay, and how is LogRecord typed?
answer_hinglish:
LogRecord ek TypeScript discriminated union hai: { op: 'code.save'; code } | { op: 'code.used'; codeHash } | ... | { op: 'session.delete'; sid }. Har variant ka 'op' literal hai, toh switch (r.op) mein TypeScript har case mein sahi fields jaanta hai, aur naya op add karke apply mein case bhoolo toh default branch StoreCorruptError throw karta hai.

apply(mem, r) record ko in-memory stores par lagata hai (MemoryCodeStore.save/consume, MemoryTokenStore.createFamily/revokeFamily/..., MemorySessionStore.save/delete). Live path: commit() pehle disk par likhta hai, phir isi apply() ko bulata hai. Replay: readLog() har line parse karke isi apply() ko bulata hai. Compaction ke baad bhi records fresh memory mein isi se replay hote hain.

Fayda: live state aur replayed state ka divergence (sabse bura persistence bug -- 'restart ke baad behaviour alag') structurally mushkil ho jaata hai. Agar replay ka alag code hota, toh ek field bhoolna ya order badalna restart ke baad hi dikhta. Restart tests (persistence.test.ts) aur mutations M17-M19 (record log na karna) dikhate hain ki jo memory mein hai woh log mein bhi hona chahiye.
why_needed: Event sourcing ka basic rule: state = apply(events); do alag implementations mat rakho.
real_world_analogy: Recipe book: khana banate waqt aur dobara banate waqt same recipe -- alag recipes = alag swaad.
how_it_works: commit(rec): durable -> apply(live, rec). readLog: JSON.parse -> apply(mem, rec).
in_this_project: src/file-store.ts LogRecord, apply, readLog, openFileStores.
advantages: Live aur replay kabhi alag nahi
disadvantages: Schema version field nahi; format change ka migration plan nahi
common_mistakes: Replay ke liye alag parser/logic
Unknown op ko ignore karna
follow_up_questions: Log format version kaise add karoge?
Event sourcing aur yeh design mein kya fark hai?

question: Compaction drops expired authorization codes. What subtle behaviour change does that cause for a reused code after a restart, and is it acceptable?
answer_hinglish:
In-memory store mein code expire hone ke baad bhi entry rehti hai. Agar koi expired-but-redeemed code dobara aaye toh consume() 'reused' deta hai aur codeGrant us code ki family revoke karta hai (RFC 6749 4.1.2: code reuse par tokens revoke SHOULD).

File store compaction start par 'e.code.expiresAt > now' wale codes hi rakhta hai. Toh restart ke baad ek expired code ka record gayab: woh code dobara aaye toh 'missing' -> invalid_grant, lekin family revoke NAHI hoti. Matlab restart ke paar, 60 s se purane leaked code ka reuse signal kho jaata hai.

Kya acceptable hai? Code 60 s ka hai; reuse detection ka main window code redeem hone ke kuch hi second baad hota hai (attacker aur client race karte hain). 60 s ke baad leaked code se attacker ko token waise bhi nahi milta (missing/expired). Jo khota hai woh sirf ek 'detection' signal hai, protection nahi. Alternative: used codes ko unke family ki lifetime tak rakho -- zyada storage. Maine simplicity chuni; yeh answer interview mein honestly batana chahiye kyunki yeh stage 1 ke 'reuse revokes' behaviour se ek corner case par alag hai aur abhi iska dedicated test nahi hai.
why_needed: Cleanup policies security signals ko chupchap badal sakti hain; unhe consciously chunna padta hai.
real_world_analogy: CCTV footage 7 din baad delete: chori rukti nahi, bas purani chori ka saboot nahi milta.
how_it_works: snapshot: codes.filter(expiresAt > now) -> expired code records log se gayab -> consume returns missing.
in_this_project: src/file-store.ts snapshot; src/server.ts codeGrant (reused branch).
advantages: Expired secrets ke hashes disk se gayab
disadvantages: Restart ke baad purane code ka reuse family revoke nahi karta
Is corner case ka test nahi
common_mistakes: Cleanup ko 'harmless' maan lena
Har cheez hamesha rakhna
follow_up_questions: Used codes kitni der rakhne chahiye?
Is case ka test kaise likhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Simplicity aur small log vs ek detection signal; protection same rehta hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Attacker 60 s se zyada wait karke restart ke baad reuse kare: kuch nahi milta, aur alert bhi nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Used codes ko family expiry tak retain karna; ya family id ke saath tombstone.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Database mein yeh ek TTL policy decision hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Retention policy document + test; reuse events ka audit log.

question: The server has been running for weeks. What grows in memory and on disk, and when is it cleaned up?
answer_hinglish:
In-memory store (bina DATA_DIR): MemoryCodeStore, MemoryTokenStore (families, refresh tokens, access-token jti records), MemorySessionStore, MemoryTransactionStore aur ctx.failures -- koi sweep nahi. Expired entries restart tak memory mein. Har token issue = naya jti record, har refresh = naya refresh entry. Lambe chalne par memory barabar badhti hai. README 'expiry sweeping while running' ko NOT implemented mein rakhta hai.

File store (DATA_DIR): wahi memory structures plus store.jsonl jo har change par badhta hai. Cleanup sirf start par compaction mein: expired codes, refresh tokens, access records, sessions aur unreferenced families hat jaate hain. Process restart nahi hua toh log aur memory dono badhte rahenge, aur agla start utna hi lamba replay karega. Login transactions jo kabhi complete nahi hue (user ne form chhod diya) memory mein reh jaate hain -- woh expire hote hain lekin delete sirf tab jab koi unhe use kare.

Operational answer: abhi ke liye periodic restart (compaction) ek workaround hai; sahi fix ek runtime sweep (timer jo expired entries hataye) aur size-based compaction. Kitni memory per token lagti hai -- measure nahi kiya, isliye koi number nahi.
why_needed: Memory leaks auth servers mein slow outages banate hain.
real_world_analogy: Office ki filing cabinet: koi purani files nahi phenkta, toh har saal ek naya cabinet.
how_it_works: Maps grow; file store compaction only in openFileStores.
in_this_project: src/store.ts Memory* classes; src/file-store.ts snapshot, openFileStores; README NOT implemented.
disadvantages: Unbounded growth
Restart par lamba replay
common_mistakes: Sweep ke bina production mein chalana
Compaction ko runtime mein bina locking ke karna
follow_up_questions: Runtime sweep ka design kya hoga?
Memory usage kaise monitor karoge?

question: Why did stage 2 add peek() to MemoryCodeStore instead of calling consume() from the file store and logging afterwards?
answer_hinglish:
Write-ahead ka rule: pehle disk, phir memory. MemoryCodeStore.consume() khud memory badalta hai (e.used = true). Agar file store pehle consume() bulata aur phir log likhta, toh disk write fail hone par memory 'used' aur disk 'unused' -- restart ke baad code dobara redeem ho sakta.

Isliye peek(codeHash) add hua: sirf padhta hai, kuch nahi badalta. File store ka consume: e = live.codes.peek(hash); missing -> return; e.used -> reused return (koi write nahi); warna commit({op: 'code.used'}) -- jo durable() ke baad apply() se memory mein consume() karta hai. markUsed ke liye getRefresh pehle se read-only tha, toh wahan naya method nahi chahiye tha. entries(), allFamilies(), allRefresh(), allAccess(), all() snapshot ke liye read-only accessors hain.

Yeh sab synchronous hai, toh peek aur commit ke beech koi request nahi aa sakti -- atomicity bani rehti hai. Lesson: ek existing 'do-it-all' method (check + mutate) ko read aur write mein todna padta hai jab beech mein ek durable step chahiye. M16 mutation ne dikhaya ki is order ka test bhi structure par nirbhar hai: write-ahead test tab hi kaam karta hai jab failure write step ke andar ho.
why_needed: Existing APIs ko naye guarantee (durability) ke liye reshape karna padta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank teller pehle balance dekhta hai (peek), ledger mein likhta hai, tab cash deta hai -- pehle cash dena aur baad mein likhna nahi.
how_it_works: peek (read) -> decide -> commit (durable + apply).
in_this_project: src/store.ts MemoryCodeStore.peek, entries; src/file-store.ts codes.consume.
advantages: Write-ahead possible bina memory store logic duplicate kiye
disadvantages: Memory store par extra methods jo interface mein nahi
common_mistakes: Pehle mutate phir log
peek aur commit ke beech await
follow_up_questions: Interface mein peek kyun nahi daala?
Database store mein yeh pattern kaisa dikhega?

question: How do JWKS caching by clients and the server's Cache-Control: max-age=300 interact with key rotation timing? What must hold between those numbers?
answer_hinglish:
Clients /jwks ko cache karte hain: hamara response 'public, max-age=300' bhejta hai, aur libraries apna cache rakhti hain (jose: cacheMaxAge aur unknown kid par reload, lekin 30 s cooldown ke baad hi). Rotation ke do moments hain jahan caches matter karte hain.

(1) Nayi key ka sign karna shuru karna: verifier ka cache purana ho toh unknown kid. Isliye next key pre-published hai: woh pichhli rotation (ya first start) se JWKS mein hai. Shart: next key kam se kam ek cache lifetime (300 s, aur libraries ke apne caches) pehle publish honi chahiye -- yahan pre-publication ka window poora rotation interval hai (default 30 din), toh shart aasani se poori.

(2) Purani key hatana: retired key retention = sabse lambi token lifetime (300 s). Hatane ke baad ek cached JWKS mein purani key reh bhi jaaye toh koi nuksan nahi -- uske tokens expire ho chuke. Ulta, agar ek client ka cache NAYA hai aur purana token laaye -- retention ke andar purani key published hai, toh verify.

Interop test yeh dikhata hai: jose cache rotation se pehle fetch, rotation ke baad naya token bina refetch verify, retention ke baad fresh fetch par purana kid JWKSNoMatchingKey. Agar rotate() do baar bahut jaldi chale (300 s ke andar), toh next key ka pre-publish window chhota hoga -- operator ko yeh dhyan rakhna hai; code isko enforce nahi karta.
why_needed: Key rotation outage zyaadatar caching assumptions ki galti se aata hai.
real_world_analogy: Naye phone number ki khabar: sabko pehle batao, phir purana number band karo -- aur purana tab tak chalu rakho jab tak pending calls khatam na hon.
how_it_works: published(): active, next, retired (not expired). JWKS response max-age=300. jose: cache + cooldown.
in_this_project: src/server.ts route (/jwks Cache-Control), keyRetentionMs; src/keys.ts FileKeyRing; test/interop.test.ts rotation test.
disadvantages: Back-to-back manual rotations ka guard nahi
common_mistakes: JWKS ko no-store karna (load) ya bahut lamba cache (rotation slow)
Nayi key ko sign ke saath hi publish
follow_up_questions: Minimum gap between rotations ko enforce karoge?
Client 24 h JWKS cache kare toh kya?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Lamba cache = kam load, lekin pre-publish window zyada chahiye. Chhota cache = zyada fetches.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Client hard-coded key use kare (JWKS fetch nahi): rotation par toot jaayega. Do rotations 300 s mein: cache wale clients ko unknown kid.
advanced.alternatives: Signed JWKS ya OpenID Federation; push notifications nahi hain spec mein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: JWKS endpoint CDN se serve ho sakta hai kyunki public hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Rotation ke minimum gap ka check, JWKS fetch metrics, unknown-kid errors ka monitoring.

question: Production scenario: you suspect the active signing key in keys.json was copied by an attacker. Walk through the incident response with what this server supports today and what is missing.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle impact: jiske paas private key hai woh kisi bhi user ke liye valid access tokens aur id_tokens bana sakta hai jo hamare /jwks se verify honge. Hamara /userinfo forged token ko reject karega agar uska jti record nahi (familyOfAccessToken undefined -> 401) -- yeh ek accidental defence hai, lekin third-party APIs jo offline verify karti hain unhe pata nahi chalega. id_tokens se attacker clients mein login kar sakta hai.

Aaj kya kar sakte ho: (1) rotate() se nayi key active -- lekin compromised key 'retired' ban ke 300 s aur published rahegi, aur hamara code use turant hatane ka command nahi deta. (2) Server band karo, keys.json edit karke compromised key hata do (ya poori file delete -- nayi keys generate hongi), restart. FileKeyRing.open 'exactly one active' check karta hai, toh edit dhyan se. Side effect: us key se sign hue saare legit tokens bhi turant invalid -- users ko 5 minute tak errors, refresh tokens (opaque) phir bhi kaam karenge aur naye tokens nayi key se. (3) Agar attacker ke paas data dir tha, toh store.jsonl bhi -- usme sirf hashes hain, raw tokens nahi.

Missing (README NOT implemented): emergency revoke command, keys encrypted at rest / KMS, access audit, alerting. Root cause bhi dhoondho: backup, container image, file permissions (Windows par mode ka koi asar nahi; Linux par M29 mode test chala aur 0644 ko pakadta hai).
why_needed: Key compromise auth server ka worst case hai; plan pehle se hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Master key chori: taala turant badlo, chahe sab residents ko nayi chaabi lene mein takleef ho.
how_it_works: Rotate (soft) vs stop + edit keys.json (hard) -> restart -> new JWKS.
in_this_project: src/keys.ts FileKeyRing.rotate, open (validation); README NOT implemented (emergency removal); test/keys.test.ts.
advantages: Keys ek file mein, manual removal possible
Store leak se raw tokens nahi milte
disadvantages: Koi one-command emergency removal nahi
Third parties forged tokens accept karengi jab tak key published
common_mistakes: Sirf rotate karke compromised key ko retention tak published chhod dena
Root cause dhoondhe bina nayi key usi jagah rakhna
follow_up_questions: Emergency removal API kaisa design karoge?
Clients ko force-refresh JWKS kaise karwaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Hard removal = security, cost: legit tokens instantly invalid. Soft rotation = smooth, cost: 300 s exposure.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Attacker ke paas key aur data dir dono: woh rotate ke baad nayi keys.json bhi padh sakta agar access abhi bhi hai -- pehle access band karo.
advanced.alternatives: KMS/HSM jahan key export hi nahi ho sakti; short-lived keys; signed key attestations.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Kai instances mein har instance ko ek saath nayi key chahiye -- central key store ke bina namumkin.
advanced.production_improvements: removeKey(kid) command, audit logs, KMS, runbook with tested steps, alert on unexpected kid in logs.

question: Automatic key rotation runs inside signing(), i.e. during a token request. What happens if saving keys.json fails at that moment?
answer_hinglish:
FileKeyRing.signing(now) dekhta hai: active key ki umar >= rotateAfterMs toh this.rotate(now). Matlab rotation kisi token request ke andar hoti hai -- jo pehli request interval ke baad aaye. rotate() naya key list banata hai, phir save() (temp file 0600, writeSync, fsyncSync, renameSync). Agar save throw kare (disk full, permission), toh catch mein this.keys = before (purani list wapas) aur error rethrow.

Phir: sendTokens ke andar exception -> route ka catch -> 500 server_error 'internal error'. Memory purani keys par hai, file bhi purani (rename nahi hua), toh state consistent. Lekin agli har token request phir rotation try karegi (active abhi bhi purani hai) aur fail hogi -- matlab disk ki problem token endpoint ka outage ban jaati hai, jabki purani key se sign karte rehna technically possible tha.

Yeh path test nahi hua (README/interview AUTH-033 mein 'test nahi kiya' likha hai). Better design options: rotation ko request path se hata ke timer ya CLI se chalana; ya save fail par log karke purani key se sign karte rehna (availability), aur alert. Interview mein point: background maintenance ko request path mein daalna simple hai lekin failures ko user-facing bana deta hai.
why_needed: Hidden work inside a request path is a classic source of surprise outages.
real_world_analogy: Cashier har 30 din baad pehle customer ke saath register badalta hai; naya register jam ho gaya toh line ruk gayi, jabki purane se kaam chal sakta tha.
how_it_works: signing -> rotate -> save throws -> keys restored -> exception -> 500; repeats every request.
in_this_project: src/keys.ts FileKeyRing.signing, rotate, save; src/server.ts sendTokens, createAuthHandler catch.
advantages: Memory aur file consistent rehte hain
disadvantages: Disk failure = token endpoint outage
Yeh path test nahi hua
common_mistakes: Save fail par memory mein nayi keys rakhna (restart par alag keys)
Rotation ko request path mein bina timeout
follow_up_questions: Rotation ko background mein kaise le jaoge?
Is failure ka test kaise likhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: In-request rotation: koi scheduler nahi chahiye; cost: failures user requests par.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Read-only filesystem, full disk, permission change: har token request 500.
advanced.alternatives: Timer/cron rotation, CLI rotate command, ya KMS-managed rotation.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Kai instances: ek hi time par sab rotate karne ki koshish karenge -- leader chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Fallback to current key with alert, test for save failure, metrics on rotation.
